Metadata.title: EmbedKit · Embedded Toolbox
Metadata.description: Online tools for firmware and protocol work: number bases, bitfields, CRC, frame checksums, cloud platform credentials. Everything runs locally in your browser — no data is uploaded.

Home.title: Embedded Toolbox
Home.intro: Online tools for MCU, protocol and debugging work: register bitfields, byte streams, checksum algorithms, cloud platform credentials. Pure client-side — your data never leaves the browser.
Home.plannedNote: Grey cards are not implemented yet. No fake doors — a tool lights up only when it works.
Home.external: {count, plural, one {# external tool} other {# external tools}}
Home.privacyNote: All computation happens in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded.

base-converter.name: Number Base Converter
base-converter.desc: Binary / octal / decimal / hex conversion with big integers, two's complement by bit width and byte order views.

crc.name: CRC Calculator
crc.desc: 24 presets (CRC-8/16/32/32C/64, Modbus, CCITT…) plus custom parameters and whole-frame CRC checks.

bitfield.name: Bitfield / Register Viewer
bitfield.desc: Inspect a register bit by bit, toggle / set / clear, and emit HEX plus C macros.

unit-converter.name: Unit Converter
unit-converter.desc: Frequency & period, storage, data rate, voltage/current and ADC codes — everyday embedded unit conversions in one place.

hex-ascii.name: HEX ↔ ASCII / C array
hex-ascii.desc: Convert between hex and text, and generate a round-trippable uint8_t array.

onenet-mqtt.name: OneNET MQTT Credentials
onenet-mqtt.desc: Generate the MQTT credential triplet, thing-model topics and runnable ESP-AT commands.

serial.name: Web Serial Monitor
serial.desc: Talk to a serial port from the browser: HEX / text / ANSI logs, packet merging, quick commands, auto-reconnect.

modbus-frame.name: Modbus Frame Builder
modbus-frame.desc: Build RTU and TCP read/write frames with automatic CRC16 and MBAP header.

pin-lookup.name: Chip Pin Lookup
pin-lookup.desc: Enter a part number and jump to PinAtlas for the pinout, alternate functions and AF numbers.

UnitConverter.freqLead: Enter either side and the other is computed live from T = 1/f. Handy for timer ticks, baud clocks and sample rates.
UnitConverter.storageLead: Embedded memory and flash are strictly binary: 1 KB = 1024 B = 8192 bit.
UnitConverter.storageNote: Mind the convention: drive and network labels are decimal (1000-based), so a 128 GB stick shows about 119 GB in the OS.
UnitConverter.rateLead: Bit-based units are strictly decimal (1000-based), and bits differ from bytes by 8: 1 KB/s = 8 kbps.
UnitConverter.rateNote: 115200 bps UART ≈ 14400 B/s; a 100 Mbps link caps at 12.5 MB/s.
UnitConverter.electricLead: 1000-based ladders for V / mV / μV and A / mA / μA; results show only the matching dimension.
UnitConverter.adcLead: Full scale maps as V = code ÷ (2ⁿ − 1) × Vref, matching the STM32 reference manual.
UnitConverter.emptyHint: Type a number and results update live.
UnitConverter.errorPositive: This conversion divides, so the value must be greater than 0.
UnitConverter.errorNegative: Capacity and data rate cannot be negative.
UnitConverter.adcRawRange: The code must be between 0 and {max}.
UnitConverter.radixText: HEX / DEC / BIN / OCT conversion, two's complement and byte-order views live in the dedicated base converter, with BigInt support.

OneNet.lead: Device info → credential triplet (signed token) → an ESP-AT command sequence you can paste into a serial console. All local to your browser.
OneNet.deviceKeyPlaceholder: the device key from the OneNET console
OneNet.deviceKeyNote: Used for the HMAC in this browser only — never uploaded, but saved on this device. Press Reset on a shared machine.
OneNet.methodNote: version is fixed at 2018-10-31 by the spec.
OneNet.expirePastWarning: That time is already in the past — the signed token would expire immediately. Pick a new time, or clear it to use “now + 30 days”.
OneNet.expireNote: Local timezone; empty means now + 30 days.
OneNet.emptyHint: Fill in the device fields, then hit “Generate MQTT parameters”.
OneNet.paramsHint: Only the params object — the tool adds the outer id and params wrapper. Types come from the JSON itself: 25.6 is a number, quoted text is a string, true is a boolean.
OneNet.paramsEmpty: The property payload cannot be empty.
OneNet.paramsInvalidJson: Not valid JSON. Keys need double quotes and there must be no trailing comma.
OneNet.paramsNotObject: The top level must be a JSON object — key/value pairs inside braces. Arrays, numbers and strings are rejected.
OneNet.atHint: Generate the MQTT parameters first — the AT commands embed the token.
OneNet.topicsNote: Identifiers and functions depend on your OneNET product.
OneNet.noteLocal: Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded. What you type — including the device key and Wi-Fi password — is saved on this device, so press Reset on a shared machine.
OneNet.noteBytes: Report length is counted in UTF-8 bytes (AT+MQTTPUBRAW wants bytes — a CJK character is 3).
OneNet.noteEspAt: AT commands target ESP-AT (ESP8266 / ESP32) firmware; leave time between commands for responses.
OneNet.notePreset: AceV67og0i / humi_temp are just demo values — swap in your own.

atBlock.publish: Property report (two separate sends, one line at a time)
atBlock.reply: Property set reply (two separate sends, one line at a time)

error.badKey: The device key is not valid Base64
error.noWebCrypto: Web Crypto is unavailable (needs https or localhost)

Serial.lead: Talk to a serial port straight from the browser — everything stays on your machine. Sent and received data both land in the log on the left.
Serial.unsupported: This browser has no Web Serial support. Use desktop Chrome or Edge (Safari and Firefox don't ship it).
Serial.openHint: Port selected — press “Open port” to start.
Serial.settingsNote: Changing settings while open reopens the port (Web Serial cannot change them live).
Serial.mergeGapNote: Chunks arriving within this gap are merged into one line; 0 disables merging.
Serial.emptyLog: Once the port is open, everything sent and received shows up here, one line per packet.
Serial.sendHint: Open the port first to send
Serial.presetsNote: Click to send; entries marked HEX are parsed as hex.
Serial.configNote: Port settings, display options and quick commands live in your browser and can be exported.
Serial.noteLocal: Data only travels between this browser and the local port — no server involved, EmbedKit has no backend.
Serial.noteHex: HEX mode shows raw bytes (use it for binary protocols); text mode decodes UTF-8.
Serial.noteAnsi: ANSI mode renders colour escapes from device logs (via ansi_up, HTML escaped).
Serial.noteReconnect: Unplugging shows “Disconnected”; replugging reconnects with the last settings unless you closed it by hand.
Serial.noteLimit: The log keeps the last 200 entries so long captures don't freeze the page.

error.oddLength: Hex length is odd — a byte needs two digits
error.noAuthorizedPort: No authorised port yet — use “Select port”

BaseConverter.lead: Type an integer in any base, get all four bases instantly, plus two's complement and byte order for the selected bit width.
BaseConverter.emptyHint: Type a value above — all four bases appear as you type.

error.prefixMismatch: The 0{prefix} prefix conflicts with the selected base ({radix})

BaseConverter.noteInteger: Integer math uses BigInt, so nothing is lost to floating point; bits above the selected width are truncated.
BaseConverter.noteCopy: Copied values carry no separators — paste them straight into code.

HexAscii.lead: Pick text, HEX or a C array as input — get HEX, text, a paste-ready uint8_t array and a hexdump.

placeholder.text: Text to convert, e.g. Hello 温度
placeholder.carray: Paste a uint8_t array from your C code

HexAscii.encodingNote: In UTF-8 a CJK character takes 3 bytes; Latin-1 is one byte per character, handy for inspecting raw bytes.
HexAscii.emptyHint: Type something — HEX, text and the C array appear as you go.
HexAscii.cArrayNote: Paste it straight into C; paste this output back into the C array input to read it again.
HexAscii.noteLocal: Everything is computed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
HexAscii.noteEncoding: HEX and the C array always work on bytes; only the text view depends on the encoding.
HexAscii.noteRoundTrip: The C array input mode parses a uint8_t array declaration copied straight out of your code, and ignores comments.
HexAscii.noteHexdump: The hexdump follows the xxd layout: offset + 16 bytes per line + |printable ASCII|.

error.oddLength: HEX length is odd — one byte needs two digits
error.badChar: “{char}” is not a valid hex digit
error.outOfRange: “{detail}” does not fit in one byte (0-255)

Crc.lead: Feed in text or HEX, then pick a preset or set poly / init / refin / refout / xorout yourself. In HEX mode, pasting a whole frame also checks its trailing CRC.
Crc.placeholderText: Text to run the CRC over
Crc.placeholderHex: Bytes to run the CRC over, e.g. 01 03 00 00 00 0A
Crc.customNote: Same notation as the reveng catalogue: poly omits the leading term (CRC-32 is 0x04C11DB7). Accepts 0x-prefixed or decimal values.
Crc.emptyHint: Type some data and the CRC appears automatically.
Crc.frameCheckNote: Once enabled, the trailing bytes are read as the frame's CRC; feeding in plain data will report a mismatch, which is expected.
Crc.frameOk: ✓ Trailing CRC matches the computed value
Crc.frameBad: ✗ Trailing CRC does not match the recomputed value: either the frame's CRC is wrong, or the input never carried one
Crc.noteLibrary: The CRC algorithms come from js-crc, whose model catalogue is generated from the reveng CRC catalogue; this tool only picks models, formats results and verifies whole frames.
Crc.noteCheck: Every preset is unit-tested against its official check value (the CRC of ASCII “123456789”), so a wrong model fails loudly.
Crc.noteZero: Handy trick: for frames that append their CRC (Modbus RTU and friends), running the CRC over the whole frame should give 0x0000.
Crc.noteLocal: Everything is computed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

error.oddLength: HEX length is odd — one byte needs two digits
error.badChar: “{char}” is not a valid hex digit
error.badParam: poly / init / xorout must be valid integers

Modbus.buildLead: Fill in the parameters and the complete frame appears: RTU appends CRC16, TCP adds the MBAP header.

modeNote.rtu: RTU: unit id + PDU + CRC16 (little endian) — serial / RS-485.
modeNote.tcp: TCP: MBAP header (transaction, protocol, length, unit id) + PDU — Ethernet.

Modbus.valuesCoilNote: Packed into bytes in order, least significant bit first; the quantity is the number of values.
Modbus.valuesNote: Space or comma separated, each 0 - 0xFFFF; the quantity is the number of values.
Modbus.quantityNote: For read requests the quantity must be {min} - {max}.
Modbus.emptyHint: Fill in the parameters and the frame shows up here.
Modbus.noteRtu: The CRC is CRC-16/MODBUS (the same model as in the CRC calculator), appended little-endian.
Modbus.noteLimits: Quantity limits come from the spec: 2000 read coils, 1968 write coils, 125 read registers, 123 write registers.
Modbus.noteLocal: Everything is computed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Modbus.parseLead: Paste a received frame (or one you just built) to break it down as RTU / TCP and verify its CRC.
Modbus.parseNote: The RTU CRC is only verified, never rewritten; exception responses (high bit set on the function code) are flagged.
Modbus.crcBad: ✗ CRC16 check failed: the frame was altered, or the wrong mode is selected
Modbus.exception: The slave returned an exception response, code {code}

error.badUnitId: Unit ID must be an integer between 0 and 255
error.badTransactionId: Transaction ID must be an integer between 0 and 65535
error.badAddress: Address must be an integer between 0 and 65535
error.emptyValues: Writing multiple values needs at least one value
error.tooShort: The frame is too short to be valid
error.badProtocolId: The MBAP protocol ID must be 0, got {detail}
error.badLength: The MBAP length field does not match the frame size (length field is {detail})
error.oddLength: HEX length is odd — one byte needs two digits
error.badChar: “{char}” is not a valid hex digit

Bitfield.lead: Click the cells to set, clear or flip individual bits and watch HEX, BIN, decimal and the two's-complement reading update; name your fields and export C macros.
Bitfield.gridNote: Left to right runs from the most significant bit down; click a cell to flip that bit.
Bitfield.signBitSet: The top bit (bit {width}) is 1, so as a {width}-bit two's-complement value this is negative.
Bitfield.signBitClear: The top bit (bit {width}) is 0, so as a {width}-bit two's-complement value this is non-negative.
Bitfield.fieldsNote: Give a name and a bit range (MSB : LSB); the extracted value shows up as you type.

fieldError.badRange: MSB must be greater than or equal to LSB
fieldError.outOfWidth: The bit range must stay within 0 - {width}

Bitfield.macrosNote: Paste straight into a header; absolute masks are used, so no shift arithmetic is needed.
Bitfield.noteClick: All bit twiddling happens locally with BigInt; the width only affects display and truncation.
Bitfield.noteSigned: HEX, BIN and decimal are the unsigned view; the signed row reads it as a {width}-bit two's-complement value.
Bitfield.noteLocal: Everything is computed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

PinLookup.lead: Enter a part number, get a PinAtlas deep link, open it in a new tab. This site holds no pin data and makes no requests.
PinLookup.chipNote: Use the dataset's ID form: the package and temperature grade become a lowercase x, e.g. STM32F103C8Tx — not the orderable part number STM32F103C8T6.
PinLookup.suggestion: That is an orderable part number. The dataset uses {suggested} — switch to it?
PinLookup.pinNote: Fills in the pin detail view.
PinLookup.variantNote: Switches between packages of the same die.
PinLookup.examplesNote: Every one of these was checked against the PinAtlas dataset and resolves directly.
PinLookup.emptyHint: Enter a part number and the target URL shows up here.
PinLookup.noteExternal: Pin data comes from PinAtlas ({origin}); EmbedKit deliberately does not maintain a second copy.
PinLookup.noteFormat: The dataset uses x to stand in for the package and temperature grade; pasting an orderable part number makes PinAtlas silently fall back to its default chip, so this page suggests the fix.
PinLookup.noteData: About 2700 chips and 310k pins, covering the mainstream STM32 families.
PinLookup.notePrivacy: Nothing happens until you press the button — this page itself makes no requests.

error.badChip: “{detail}” is not a valid part number (letters, digits and . _ - + only)
error.badPin: “{detail}” is not a valid pin name
error.badVariant: “{detail}” is not a valid package name

NotFound.title: Page not found
NotFound.desc: There is no tool page at this address. The link may be wrong, or the tool is not built yet.

Error.title: This tool hit an error
Error.desc: The page threw an exception in your browser. Try again first; if it keeps failing, reload the page.
